solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spies seize retreating councillor roughly

indicators.note: to seize is to hold, so the spies' letters clasp the other piece inside them

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency, a body of spies

indicators.note: something retreating goes backwards, so the abbreviation is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Secret agents grab a local councillor who is backing away, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' reverses the abbreviation before 'seize' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin preposition is used before dates and figures to mean approximately or about.

clue.text: Press award supported by directors

indicators.note: in a down answer a piece supported by another sits above it

parts.note: a cup is an award or trophy
a board is a company's body of directors

explanation.surface: A prize for journalism is backed by the directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' suggests newspapers; it is a cabinet, as in an airing press.
explanation.definitionFit: A press is a cabinet or recessed storage unit with shelves, especially in Irish and Scottish use.

clue.text: Call inspires revolutionary story telling

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the call takes the story inside it

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the story word is read backwards

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A phone call inspires a tale of revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' signals reversal here, not rebellion; 'inspires' (breathes in) signals containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating events is narrating them, telling them to someone.

clue.text: Televise cunning US chef's big vessel

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast or televise it
craft means cunning or guile
Robert Carrier was an American-born cookery writer and chef famous in Britain

explanation.surface: Broadcasting a crafty American cook's big pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a cooking pot in a chef's surface; it is a warship.
explanation.definitionFit: A warship with a flight deck from which planes take off is a very big vessel.

clue.text: Struggle with drink, adopting old attitude

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the drink takes the abbreviation for old inside it

parts.note: a pint is a drink of beer

explanation.surface: Someone battling alcohol takes up an old-fashioned outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A point of view is an attitude or standpoint on a matter.

clue.text: Old magistrate briefly brought up wind

indicators.note: in a down answer, brought up means read from the bottom upwards
briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the official's title is dropped

parts.note: a reeve was a medieval local magistrate or official

explanation.surface: A former magistrate is briefly mentioned in connection with wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts REEVE to REEV; 'brought up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind is to twist and turn, as a road does when it changes direction suddenly.

clue.text: With which to pick up sound of jumbo in Bow?

definitions.text: With which to pick up sound of jumbo in Bow?

indicators.note: Bow is in the East End of London, where Cockneys drop the letter H

parts.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it
an elephant's call is a trumpet

explanation.surface: How a deaf Londoner might catch an elephant's call.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys (from Bow, East London) drop their aitches, so HEAR becomes EAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The old horn-shaped hearing aid helped the hard of hearing pick up sounds.

clue.text: Inconspicuous US officer scuppers slot machine plan

indicators.note: to scupper is to wreck, so these letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A one-armed bandit thwarts a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: An American detective who wears ordinary clothes rather than uniform is undercover and inconspicuous.

clue.text: This writer's going round to stay in the same place

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so the writer's letters surround the other piece

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to himself: I'M, I am
to bide is to stay or remain

explanation.surface: An author circles back to stay put in one place.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word, used in references to cite the work just cited, means in that same place.

clue.text: Unrestricted hard nuts head up Arctic region

indicators.note: in a down answer heading up means reading from the bottom upwards
without restriction means losing the outer limits, so the letters inside the phrase, minus its first and last, are taken

explanation.surface: Tough characters roam freely and head north to the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unrestricted' strips H and S from 'hard nuts', leaving ARDNUT; 'head up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The treeless frozen plain of northern Russia and Canada is a typical Arctic landscape.

clue.text: Seal hunter directly opposite harbour

parts.note: polar opposites are directly opposed, so polar means directly opposite
to harbour a grudge is to bear it

explanation.surface: A seal-hunting boat lies just across from the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: The great white Arctic carnivore preys chiefly on seals, so it is a seal hunter.

clue.text: A food item chopped for birds

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: relating to birds

indicators.note: chopped means cut short, so the final letter of the food word is lopped off

parts.note: a viand is an item of food

explanation.surface: A bit of food is cut up to feed the birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped' removes the last letter from VIAND, leaving VIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to birds, from the Latin avis.

clue.text: Court disputed jury's conclusion, causing hoo-ha

indicators.note: something disputed is contested and thrown into question, so these letters are rearranged
the conclusion of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A court challenged the jury's verdict, and there was a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disputed' rearranges COURT to OUTCR; Y is the last letter of 'jury's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A public protest or uproar is a hoo-ha, a noisy commotion.

clue.text: Monarchs (father and child) embody uniform pomp

parts.note: GR, George Rex, is the royal cipher of George VI, the father

indicators.note: to embody is to contain within, so the monarchs' letters hold the uniform letter

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of his daughter Elizabeth II
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A royal father and daughter display all the pomp of uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: George VI was father of Elizabeth II, hence the two royal ciphers; 'embody' places the uniform letter inside the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour and magnificence are the essence of pomp and ceremony.

clue.text: So-called trick cyclist to stop shooting film

parts.note: trick cyclist is old slang for a psychiatrist, also called a shrink
in film-making, 'it's a wrap' declares the end of shooting

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist tells a stunt cyclist to halt filming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' is not a movie but thin plastic wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight plastic wrapping shrunk onto goods is a type of thin clinging film.

clue.text: Average factory manager enjoys this

definitions.meaning: a mill boss runs the factory, read literally

explanation.surface: An ordinary mill boss likes what he does.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means ordinary or unremarkable, as goods straight off the production line.

clue.text: Have no energy during run — the result of blow?

indicators.note: during means within, so the lacking pieces go inside the run

parts.note: in cricket a bye is a run scored without the ball being hit
to lack something is to have none of it
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Lacking energy on a run might come from a blow.
explanation.walkthrough: A bye is an extra run in cricket, scored when the ball passes the batter untouched.
explanation.definitionFit: A punch to the face leaves bruising round the eye, a shiner.

clue.text: Northbound, my route cuts Sydney suburbs for comfort

indicators.note: to cut into is to enter, so the pieces go inside the suburbs
the suburbs of a word are its outlying letters, its first and last
in a down answer, going north means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: a path is a route

explanation.surface: Heading north, my journey cuts through Sydney's suburbs for ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northbound' reverses 'my' to YM, since a down answer reads north as upwards; 'cuts' puts it and PATH inside the suburbs of Sydney.
explanation.definitionFit: Offering compassion for someone's sorrow is giving consolation, a form of comfort.

clue.text: By chance, stress colleague grabbing passport?

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing and holding, so the passport's letters are taken inside

parts.note: accent is stress placed on a syllable
a passport is a form of identification, ID
an ally is a colleague or partner

explanation.surface: A stressed co-worker snatches a passport, perhaps by chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done unintentionally happens by chance rather than design.

clue.text: A second English degree? That's not much of a life

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a degree

explanation.surface: A quick English degree is a poor life, someone complains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' is a link word; the life is a tiny single-celled creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-celled organism is a minimal form of living thing, so barely much of a life.

clue.text: Open a French type of sandwich with nothing in it

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: with something in it means containing it, so the sandwich holds the zero letter
completes the containment signal begun by with

parts.note: a BLT is a bacon, lettuce and tomato sandwich
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Open up a French sandwich and find it empty.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbolt a door is to draw back the bolt and so open it.

clue.text: Create circles with river plant that's toxic

indicators.note: to circle is to go around, so the making word surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: to make is to create
and means with, joining things

explanation.surface: A poisonous riverside plant grows in rings.
explanation.definitionFit: The forked-rooted plant of the nightshade family is poisonous and steeped in folklore.

clue.text: Leaves container that holds a fortune?

definitions.text: Leaves container that holds a fortune?

parts.words: Leaves container that holds a fortune?
parts.note: it holds tea leaves, and fortune-tellers read the future in the leaves left in it

explanation.surface: A vessel for leaves turns out to hold great wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' tempts towards trees or departures; here it is tea leaves, read by fortune-tellers.
explanation.definitionFit: The cup holds tea leaves, whose pattern tasseography claims tells a fortune.

clue.text: Move quickly about in south of France

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the abbreviation for about goes inside the French word

parts.note: sud is French for south
C, for circa, is an abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: Rushing around in the south of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'south of France' is not the Riviera but the French word for south, SUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Clouds scud when they race across the sky, driven quickly by the wind.

clue.text: European firm initially looks into bacteria in canal

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: initially means at the start, taking the first letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A European company first investigates bacteria in a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: The canal is the alimentary canal, the gut, not a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: Escherichia coli is a bacterium living in the human gut, the alimentary canal.

clue.text: Flat hire charge includes copper gong

indicators.note: includes means contains, so the charge word holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: rent is the charge for hiring something
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a gong is British slang for a medal or honour, such as the MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire)

explanation.surface: The charge for renting a flat includes some copper and a gong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like a home to rent; it means lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying down on one's back means lying flat, reclining.

clue.text: Devious trap-door hides head of hairy spider, say

indicators.note: devious means winding or crooked, so these letters are twisted into a new order
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A sneaky trapdoor conceals a hairy spider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hides' places H (head of 'hairy') among the letters of TRAPDOOR before 'Devious' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiders, insects and crustaceans are jointed-legged invertebrates of this phylum; 'say' marks an example.

clue.text: Born next to Derry's walls in poverty

parts.note: née means born, used of a woman's maiden name

indicators.note: the walls of a word are its outside letters

explanation.surface: Born beside the old walls of Derry into poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: Derry, in Northern Ireland, is famous for its city walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor people are in want, lacking money, which is to be in poverty.
